Subject: Realtime feed stall — production (US-west)

Stephanie —

We're seeing repeated stalls in the realtime transcript stream for our production integration this morning. The UI freezes and tokens stop arriving for 8–15s at a time; afterwards chunks resume and the session continues. This started around 08:40 PDT and has impacted ~15% of active sessions. Latency also spikes (p90 token latency up from ~120ms to 700ms) and we observed an uptick in 502/504 over the same window.

This is affecting our clinician note-taking workflow in the web app — we had to roll a portion of traffic to the polling endpoint as a temporary workaround. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (deploys, routing, CDN/proxy config) and escalate to engineering? We need an ETA for a root cause and an interim mitigation.

I've attached a short capture (ws_trace_20270507.pcap) and a condensed log bundle.

—Alexandra

Looping in with initial findings from the first 20m of traces. Summary:
- Observed repeated WebSocket keepalive timeouts between our proxy layer and the serving cluster (TCP FIN/ACKs followed by new handshake within ~10s).
- Chunked transfer shows sequences where the server stream writes a 0-length chunk (keepalive) and the proxy coalesces/blocks for ~8–12s before forwarding; downstream client sees silence.
- 5xx spike is correlated with a small fraction of requests hitting a newly scaled autoscaler bucket (cold kernels + quantization path mismatch) — those hosts respond slower and cause backpressure.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing:
1) Increase WebSocket keepalive and idle timeout on the proxy from 15s -> 35s to avoid spurious FINs while we remediate.
2) Roll traffic away from the suspect autoscaler bucket (canary hosts) for Skyline's routes.
3) Enable application-level prefix-KV caching for Skyline (low risk) to reduce load on cold hosts.
4) As a short-term customer-facing mitigation: enable polling fallback and whiteboard an SLA credit.

Rishi Malhotra
Serving Runtime Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

P.S. I've pulled the pcap and logs into the incident Drive folder and marked timestamps where the keepalive failed. Attaching a short mitigation playbook (mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf) to the incident notes.

- We'll keep the channel open and share a short RCA within 48 hours; if the RCA shows clear SLA breach we'll include a credit proposal.

I've scheduled a 30-minute incident huddle with Eng/Ops now; Rishi is leading remediation. Grace, can you prepare the customer comms summary for execs?

Subject: Re: Realtime feed stall — production (US-west) — follow-up and next steps

Alexandra — quick update and next steps after the incident huddle this morning.

What happened (short): a subset of autoscaled hosts entered a cold execution pathway while under burst; the proxy layer treated the transient slow-writes as broken streams and issued connection resets. That produced silent windows where clients received no token chunks and raised apparent 502/504 errors at the edge.

What we did (remediation):
- Immediately routed Skyline traffic off the canary bucket and onto warmed hosts (completed 09:55 PDT).
- Increased proxy WS keepalive to 35s while we test a longer-term fix.
- Enabled polling fallback on affected routes (customer-visible drop to polling observed in 12 sessions; majority recovered to streaming after host warm-up).
- Collected and shared artifacts (logs, pcap) to your team — link above.

Next steps (engineering):
- Rishi / Runtime team: finalize a patch that ensures the kernel-selection path uses warmed quantized kernels before accepting traffic (ETA: 72 hours).
- Ops: add additional health gating to avoid sending production traffic to freshly scaled hosts for latency-sensitive routes (ETA: 48 hours).

Customer ask and Redwood offer:
- We're preparing an RCA doc and credit estimate for any SLA impact. Vanessa will follow up with a formal credit proposal.
- For immediate confidence, we can schedule a short runbook walk-through and a joint test window next week (I proposed Tueday 10am PDT).

Thanks for partnering on this — we know this is disruptive. Please reply here with any additional session IDs you'd like us to prioritize.

—Stephanie
